blindWork: [Na+] = 0.200 M from Na2CO3 requires [Na2CO3] = 0.100 M since each formula unit gives two Na+. n = 0.100 M x 0.2500 L = 0.02500 mol; m = 0.02500 x 105.99 = 2.650 g.
stem: Solution Preparation: How many grams of $\text{Na}_{2}\text{CO}_{3}$ ($105.99\text{~g/mol}$) are required to prepare $250.0\text{~mL}$ of a solution with a sodium ion concentration of $0.200\text{~M}$?
sourceExplanation: $\left\lbrack \text{Na}^{+} \right\rbrack = 0.200\text{~M}$, so $\left\lbrack \text{Na}_{2}\text{CO}_{3} \right\rbrack = 0.100\text{~M}$. Moles needed $= 0.100 \times 0.250 = 0.025\text{~mol}$. Mass $= 0.025 \times 105.99 = 2.65\text{~g}$? Wait, $2 \times \text{Na}^{+}$ per mole of $\text{Na}_{2}\text{CO}_{3}$, so $\left\lbrack \text{Na}_{2}\text{CO}_{3} \right\rbrack = 0.100\text{~M}$. Moles $= 0.025$, mass $= 2.65\text{~g}$. (B)
